Lots of people in the comments keep saying to never use big negative letter spacing. I disagree. This is what I use with Geist:

16px → 0%
36px → -3%
100px+ → -5 to -6%

The “never go negative” rule is for body text. At 100px+ the default spacing looks loose, because the gaps between letters scale up with the size. Tightening them is what makes big headlines look clean.

Body text stays at 0%. The bigger the text, the tighter it gets. Nothing goes past -6%, because past that the letters start touching.

one mindset shift took me from charging $1000-$2000 per project to closing $ 50k+ deals:

I used to think $2,000 for a landing page was a lot. then I did the math.

a single full time designer, not accounting for development, animation, or anything else, just one designer, costs more than that per week.

that one realization changed everything.

suddenly $30,000 for a full project didn't feel expensive. it felt reasonable.

because when you break down what actually goes into delivering world-class work, the numbers start making a lot of sense.

as an agency you're not just paying for the person doing the design. you're paying for project managers, ops, sales, account management. people who have nothing to do with delivery but are essential to running the business.

when you factor all of that in, a $20,000/month retainer doesn't feel like a lot anymore. it's actually tight.
and when people hear $100k project, they imagine a one week sprint. it's not. it's usually a $15k/month retainer running across multiple months with a full team behind it.

spread out like that, it's incredibly reasonable for what's being delivered.

this mindset shift is what allowed us to start quoting bigger numbers with confidence and actually close those deals.

if you're still feeling uncomfortable quoting $10k, $20k, $100k projects, do the math on what it actually costs to deliver them properly.

the discomfort disappears pretty fast.

a lot of designers have been DMing me recently saying they're barely surviving in 2026.

designers who were killing it just a year or two ago. consistent clients, healthy revenue, everything going well. and now suddenly struggling to close anything.

here's what I think is happening.

the mid market is dying. the $2k-$10k project range is drying up fast.

all the money startups used to spend in the middle of the market is shifting. it's going either to the bottom end or the top end. nothing in between.

the ones going cheap, $200-$1,000, just want a slight improvement on whatever AI spat out. good enough, fast, cheap. they don't need a real designer for that.

then there's the other end. founders and companies at a later stage who want the real thing. $20k-$30k+ for a world class brand, product, or website that actually moves the needle. they're still spending. they're spending more than ever.

the in-between is disappearing.

if you're a designer stuck in the middle right now, the market is telling you something. either go premium and build the kind of portfolio that justifies $20k+ projects, or find a way to serve the bottom of the market at volume.

there's no comfortable middle ground left.
